The geometric meaning of a vector dot product is the projection of one vector onto another. It is a scalar quantity that represents the magnitude of the projection and the cosine of the angle between the vectors. The dot product of two vectors \(\mathbf{a}\) and \(\mathbf{b}\) is given by:

\[
\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = |\mathbf{a}| |\mathbf{b}| \cos \theta
\]

where \(\theta\) is the angle between the vectors. The magnitude of the projection is given by:

\[
|\text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}} \mathbf{a}| = |\mathbf{a}| \cos \theta
\]

The dot product is also equal to the product of the magnitudes of the vectors and the cosine of the angle between them:

\[
\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = |\mathbf{a}| |\mathbf{b}| \cos \theta
\]

When the vectors are orthogonal (i.e., \(\theta = 90^\circ\)), the dot product is zero. This is because the cosine of 90 degrees is zero. When the vectors are parallel (i.e., \(\theta = 0^\circ\) or \(\theta = 180^\circ\)), the dot product is the product of the magnitudes of the vectors. This is because the cosine of 0 degrees or 180 degrees is 1.

The negative projection of a vector \(\mathbf{a}\) onto another vector \(\mathbf{b}\) is given by:

\[
-\text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}} \mathbf{a} = -|\mathbf{a}| \cos \theta
\]

This is because the dot product is the product of the magnitudes of the vectors and the cosine of the angle between them, and the cosine of 180 degrees is -1.
